newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Chevron signs Venezuela aromatics plant accord.
newsitem.headline: Chevron signs Venezuela aromatics plant accord.

text.p: Chevron Chemical Company, a unit of Chevron Corp, signed a feasibility agreement with Venezuelan state oil subsidiary Maraven for a $1 billion aromatics plant to be built in Venezuela, Maraven said in a statement on Wednesday.

"This agreement confirms the confidence that major foreign investors have in Venezuela's oil and chemical sectors," said Maraven president Emilio Abouhamad, who signed the deal with John Peppercorn, president of Chevron Chemical.
The plant would be built in the Cardon refinery complex on Venezuela's north coast and it would produce 1.173 million tonnes of aromatics, feedstocks used in the plastics industry.
Abouhamad saw the agreement as another step in the opening of the Venezuelan oil sector to private capital and the industrialisation of Venezuela's refinery streams.

Chevron's Peppercorn said: "Chevron's technology and international marketing skills, combined with Maraven's raw materials and Venezuela's geographical position, provide the base for a world-class petrochemical complex."

If the project goes ahead, the investment would go towards annual output of 521,000 tonnes of para-xylene, 340,000 tonnes of benzene, 240,000 tonnes of ethyl-benzene and 63,000 tonnes hydrogen, the statement said.
